title: Latency-aware quantization recommender — heuristics & experiment plan
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a lightweight recommender and experiment plan for picking quantization profiles (INT8 / FP8 / 4-bit hybrid) per route/model given latency SLOs, quality degradation tolerance, and cost targets. The goal is to produce a small set of deterministic heuristics the UX/console can show as an initial suggestion, plus a prioritized bench plan to validate and expand the ruleset.

High-level idea (one-liner):
Given: route SLO (p95), max allowable quality delta, and token-cost target -> pick the cheapest quantization profile whose measured p95 and quality delta are within constraints for representative payloads and sequence-length mixes. If none meet constraints, suggest fallback policies (smaller model, dedicated pool, or batching change).

Assumptions & baseline constants (team to verify):
- Baseline model: Llama2-13B-like. Baseline full-precision throughput and latency numbers come from infra bench (ref linked_artifacts).
- Cost assumptions (hosted inference): 1 GPU token-cost estimate normalized: FP16 = 1.0 unit, INT8 = 0.55–0.65 units, FP8 = 0.6–0.75 units, 4-bit = 0.30–0.45 units (varies by kernel/hardware). Use conservative midpoint for initial suggestions.
- Quality proxy: dataset of 200 prompts per route (representative) -> metric = normalized log-perplexity delta and task-specific accuracy where available. We map to a single scalar: quality_delta_percent (positive means worse than baseline).
- Latency measurement: p95 end-to-end observed at target request concurrency and sequence-length mix in a synthetic bench run (include KV/prefix cache state as appropriate).

Recommender heuristics (starter rules):
1) If p95_target <= 50ms: prefer FP8 (if hardware supports low-latency FP8 kernels) or maintain FP16; only choose INT8/4-bit if prior profiling shows no quality regressions and measured p95 <= p95_target * 0.9 (i.e., headroom).
2) If 50ms < p95_target <= 200ms: INT8 is the default suggestion if quality_delta <= 1.5% and measured p95 <= p95_target. Else FP8.
3) If p95_target > 200ms: 4-bit (mixed or whole-model) is allowable as long as quality_delta <= 3% and tail latency under SLO. If model exhibits catastrophic quality drop, recommend hybrid (4-bit attention + 8-bit MLP) or enable KV/prefix caching.
4) For routes with high variance in seq-length (>50% long-tail > 1k tokens), bias suggestions to slightly higher precision (FP8/INT8) because long sequences amplify quantization errors on some models.
5) For hallucination-sensitive routes (classification, retrieval augmentation, financial/legal), default max quality_delta = 0.5% and require manual sign-off; recommender flags as "needs human review".

Quality vs latency trade heuristics (how to present to a PM/dev):
- Show triad: {estimated cost savings %, expected p95 delta ms, best-case quality_delta%}. Each number is backed by the measured bench for the model+route profile.
- Show uncertainty: 90% confidence interval based on 3 bench runs with different seeds and caching states.
- If model selection implies >15% cost savings, present an A/B rollout suggestion: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 100% with evaluation checkpoints on quality metrics and error rates.

Example candidate table (text-format; bench placeholders):
Model: Llama2-13B-like, route: completions-chatbot, seq mix: {short=70%, medium=20%, long=10%}, token-cost target: reduce 30%
- FP16 (baseline): cost=1.0x, p95=165ms, quality_delta=0.0%
- FP8 (recommended): cost=0.68x, p95=150ms, quality_delta=0.6%
- INT8: cost=0.60x, p95=140ms, quality_delta=1.8%  <-- exceed quality tolerance 1.5% -> flag
- 4-bit (full): cost=0.37x, p95=130ms, quality_delta=4.9%  <-- too high quality drop -> suggest hybrid
- 4-bit (hybrid attention-only): cost=0.48x, p95=135ms, quality_delta=1.6% <-- borderline, require canary

Decision flow (for console):
1) Collect inputs: route SLO (ms), max quality_delta_percent, traffic fraction, seq-length profile (auto-sampled), model variant list allowed.
2) Run fast profiler (micro-bench): 30s synthetic run per quant profile with sampled prompts (use warmed kv-cache if route uses it). Return p95 and quality_delta estimate (approx).
3) Apply heuristics above; propose top 2 profiles with justification strings (e.g., "FP8: 32% cost savings, p95 150ms < SLO 180ms, quality_delta 0.6% < 1.0%").
4) If both proposals fail constraints, propose operational mitigations: increase SLO, increase resource tier, enable caching, or reduce max tokens.

Profiling methodology (practical notes):
- Use representative prompt corpus per route. Put a lightweight prompt curation UX into the console (allow dev to pick 10–20 canonical prompts).
- Micro-bench config: 3 runs, 200 requests each across concurrency levels matching production (or minimal set: c=1, c=8, c=32). Measure p50/p95/p99, token throughput, tail variance.
- Quality check: run task-specific evaluation (classification accuracy, rerank NDCG, or LM NLL). For general chat, use a small set of instructive prompts and automated heuristics (QA exact match, or embedding-distance compared to reference answers).
- Important: run both cold and warmed-cache runs for stateful routes. If route uses long convo context, profile with KV cache warmed.

Edge cases & cautions:
- Some models show non-monotonic quality drop when mixed-precision applied only to MLP vs attention. Record component-level quantization sensitivity (attention/MLP/embeds).
- On some GPU stacks, 4-bit can be faster than INT8 for certain batch sizes (kernel availability). The recommender must be hardware-aware: include hardware profile mapping in metadata.
- Quantization interacts with compiler/kernels; perf measured in bench must exactly match target infra (hosted vs dedicated vs private).

Suggested UI labels to present to users:
- "Safe" — likely within quality limit and below SLO with >10% headroom
- "Canary" — within thresholds but needs traffic ramp and monitoring
- "Risky" — exceeds quality tolerance or close to SLO; requires manual review

Experiment plan (priority + owner + ETA):
- E1 (high): Implement micro-bench harness to run 5 quant profiles (FP16, FP8, INT8, 4-bit full, 4-bit hybrid) and collect metrics for 10 routes. Owner: Miguel. ETA: 3 weeks.
- E2 (medium): Build a mapping table of per-model component sensitivity (attention vs MLP) for top 12 open models we ship. Owner: Samir. ETA: 6 weeks.
- E3 (high): Integrate quick-recommender into console as "Suggest quant profile" (no auto-apply) with canary template. Owner: Ellen. ETA: 8 weeks.
- E4 (low): Add A/B rollback automation tied to quality regression alerts in Redwood Optimize. Owner: product-eng. ETA: 12 weeks.

Acceptance criteria for recommender v1:
- Recommender suggestions match human-expert pick in 8/10 internally validated routes.
- Bench runs produce stable p95 estimates (stdev < 10%) across 3 runs for recommended profile.
- Console shows clear canary rollout with automated quality checks (at least one metric: LM NLL or route-specific accuracy)

Operational checklist for QA before enabling a profile on production traffic:
- Run bench with full-length representative samples (not just short prompts).
- Validate generated-output quality on golden set; run human spot-check for hallucination-sensitive routes.
- Verify kernel/hardware map compatibility (make sure target infra has optimized kernels).

Open questions / discussion items:
- What is a defensible default for max quality_delta for general chat vs task-specific routes? (proposal: chat=1.5%, retrieval/qa=0.5%, classification=0.5%).
- How much historical traffic sampling is needed to surface representative seq-length mix? (2 weeks sampling?)
- When should we surface "hybrid quantization" vs full-model quantization as a top-line option?

Next steps (short term):
- Miguel: prototype micro-bench harness using existing infra bench scripts and share results for 3 flagship routes by 2025-02-02.
- Samir: start model component sensitivity sweep for two models and update the shared spreadsheet.
- Ellen: draft console UX copy for "Suggest quant profile" and flow for canary rollout.

Notes to self: this doc intentionally light on formal math — aim is to ship pragmatic defaults and validate with actual bench data. We should convert heuristics into a small decision tree (and eventually a compact ML model) once we have ~100 route+model+profile datapoints.

End of doc.
